newsitem.title: UK: Johnson Matthey sets auto JV with Marelli.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey sets auto JV with Marelli.

text.p: Britain's Johnson Matthey said on Thursday that it had launched a joint venture with Italian auto components group Magneti Marelli SpA to supply emission control catalysts to the growing automotive markets of South America.
In the new company, to be called Johnson Matthey Argentina SA, Johnson Matthey's Catalytic Systems Division will hold a 70 percent stake, Johnson Matthey said in a statement on Thursday.

As soon as appropriate approvals are obtained the new company, Johnson Matthey Argentina SA, will construct a facility in the Buenos Aires region with a capacity of 1.5 million pieces per year at an approximate cost of five million stg, it said.
From this base the JV will supply catalysts to the Argentinian and Brazilian car markets where vehicle production is forecast to grow by 40 percent to 2.5 million by the year 2000, it added.

"Magneti Marelli, with its expertise in the areas of fuel injection, engine management and exhaust systems, has found an ideal partner in Johnson Matthey with its world-leading catalyst technology," said Domenico Bordone, President and CEO of Magneti Marelli SpA.

Mike Cleare, Managing Director of Matthey Catalytic Systems Division, praised the opportunities that the South American markets offered, saying "South America is a major opportunity for us with its rapidly growing demand for emission control systems." -- London newsroom +44 171 542 7717
